rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Referent resolution under a sequential deck read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Chunk 1 "Big Idea": "the run you already have" is a definite reference to the student's own just-finished M4 send-off. It has not been named yet WITHIN this file (Prework, chunk 2, is what names "the un-packaged send-off artefact"), but it describes the reader's own lived state on walking into this module -- directly analogous to the exercise carve-out's own listed example "the bug from prework" (a definite reference resolved by what the student is holding, not by prior in-file text). Treated as covered by the session-artifact / module-arc-beat carve-out extended to a module's own opener framing. Chunk 2 "Prework": "the un-packaged send-off artefact", "the un-packaged session" -- session-artifact carve-out (student's own M4 output), clean. Chunk 4 "Start here": "the artefact", "the lecture below" (resolves same-chunk against the two lecture includes at lines 26/28) -- fine; "the M1 countermove" names its own claim in the same sentence ("never let the agent say everything"), doesn't require M1 recall to be understood. Chunk 5 "Your nag writes the verifier": "the un-packaged send-off" (session-artifact carve-out), "the artefact" (same); "did it touch the migration, did the tests really cover the edge" read as an illustrative rhetorical example of the SHAPE of a nagging worry, not a claim about a real named migration anywhere in the corpus -- understandable as a stand-in, not a broken referent. Chunk 6 "Set up the worktree": "what you built in Module 1 and Module 3" -- arc-earned module names (explicitly exempted, "module names"); "the two copies" resolves same-sentence (worktree fork just described); "the two closing lectures" resolves against the two includes immediately following in the same chunk. Chunk 7 "Key Concepts": "The model already knows the public field" and "a candidate, not an optimum" map to specific slides in the inlined lecture at chunk 6 (verified via grep of lectures/what-packaging-is.md: "## The model has read the field" line 221, "## Two bearings make a candidate, not an optimum" line 233) -- the lecture is included BEFORE this chunk in this file's own reading order, and the maintainer block states the mapping is deliberate ("so the reminders-only test passes by construction"). "this task, model, repository, and setup" is a generic class-level principle statement, not a specific-referent claim. Chunk 8 "Bring to Module 6": "the re-send" resolves to this module's own exercise (chunk 6's "[Exercise: Diagnose and re-send]"). Chunk 10 "Next": "Your verifier" and "one of three eval shapes" resolve to What You'll Learn's own three-shape LO (chunk 3, line 16). No never-named or vague-with-full-history referent found in the active-branch chunks.

Every cross-file reference names the source by title, not by position: "[Lecture: Reading the return]", "[Lecture: Learning through contrast]", "[Exercise: Fork the worktree, carry the evidence]", "[Exercise: Diagnose and re-send]", "[Lecture: What packaging is]", "[Lecture: The gate is a claim too]" (all structural include-links, exempt per rule 13), plus the two Prework supplementary links ("Clean Code Is Steering...", "Verification asymmetry") and four external practitioner links (Entis, Klaassen x2, da Costa), all named by title/author, none located by page position ("the opener said", "as covered above"). "The M1 countermove" (chunk 4) names the source module and unpacks the claim in the same clause rather than pointing at it positionally.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Live-demo beats survive a text read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No guess-before-reveal instruction anywhere in this file (module files are metadata/framing/sequencing surfaces; the demo beats live in the included lectures/exercises, out of this file's scope).

Every chunk carries a self-standing claim or a named set of includes with framing prose (Big Idea's thesis sentence, Prework's artefact instruction, the five What-You'll-Learn LOs, Start here's framing + blockquote, the nag beat's three-paragraph arc, Set-up-the-worktree's rationale, the four Key Concepts lines, Bring-to-Module-6's carry-forward instruction, the two pre-read annotations, Next's two-sentence bridge). None is a bare wait-state or single context-dependent bullet.

"Big Idea", "Prework", "What You'll Learn", "Key Concepts", "Next" are architecture-mandated canonical section names (curriculum/module-shape.md). "Start here", "Set up the worktree", "Pre-reads before Module 6", "Bring to Module 6" all match their chunk's content plainly. "Your nag writes the verifier" is thematic/spirit-level rather than a literal single-sentence claim (the body reads "hold the worry beside the artefact... the artefact wins" -- the nag alone doesn't write it, the artefact adjudicates); the maintainer block records that Antti reviewed and corrected this exact passage's body twice (2026-07-10, 2026-08-14) while retaining this header, which reads as deliberate spirit-not-literal titling rather than an oversight -- treated as maintainer-attested, not flagged.

No "Not X. Not Y. Z." construction, no anaphora/epistrophe triples, no self-grading superlatives, no unlabeled-number-with-retraction, no abstraction-noun stacks, no empty-leg verb triplets in any chunk. "That control pays twice" (chunk 5) is a two-item list, not a triple, and both legs (steer without babysitting; a session you don't babysit can run beside another) carry distinct concrete content.
